questions.q: The editorial says each day brings opportunities that “do not loudly announce themselves.” What must one keep in mind while using them?
options: Only large opportunities are worth taking
Not quite. The article says: Others have interests too, so one advances by cooperation and by avoiding clashes.
Others have interests too, so one advances by cooperation and by avoiding clashes
Yes. Success never comes through conflict.
Opportunities belong to whoever takes them first
Not quite. The article says: Others have interests too, so one advances by cooperation and by avoiding clashes.
It is safer to let them pass
Not quite. The article says: Others have interests too, so one advances by cooperation and by avoiding clashes.
questions.rationale: “Success in your life can happen only by cooperating with others, never through conflict… A smart person carefully avoids clashing with other people’s interests.”

questions.q: “No matter how big a palace you live in, you can occupy just one room at a time.” What does the article conclude from such remarks?
options: Wealth should be passed to one’s children early
Not quite. The article says: Take from the world only what is needed and make the Hereafter one’s aim.
Build smaller houses
Not quite. The article says: Take from the world only what is needed and make the Hereafter one’s aim.
Share one’s palace with others
Not quite. The article says: Take from the world only what is needed and make the Hereafter one’s aim.
Take from the world only what is needed and make the Hereafter one’s aim
Right. Nothing gathered here is taken along.
questions.rationale: “Wise is the one who takes from the things of the world only that which is necessary and makes the Hereafter the focus of his efforts and hopes.”

questions.q: What principle does the article say should replace “my community, right or wrong”?
options: Refusing to discuss the community at all
Not quite. The article says: Judging the community’s conduct by the teachings of the Quran, not defending whatever it does.
Judging other communities more strictly
Not quite. The article says: Judging the community’s conduct by the teachings of the Quran, not defending whatever it does.
Leaving judgement to political leaders
Not quite. The article says: Judging the community’s conduct by the teachings of the Quran, not defending whatever it does.
Judging the community’s conduct by the teachings of the Quran, not defending whatever it does
Yes. Islam and Muslims are to be distinguished.
questions.rationale: “Islam needs to be understood according to the Quranic teachings and the Muslim community should be judged in this light rather than by the principle—‘my community, right or wrong’.”

questions.q: What does the article observe about violence in the world of nature, and what does it infer?
options: Nature rewards the aggressive
Not quite. The article says: Nature works by cooperation and harmony; deliberate violence is found only among humans and brings only destruction.
Nature works by cooperation and harmony; deliberate violence is found only among humans and brings only destruction
Well read. “Violence can destroy, but not build.”
Nature is indifferent, so nothing can be learnt from it
Not quite. The article says: Nature works by cooperation and harmony; deliberate violence is found only among humans and brings only destruction.
Nature is violent, so violence is natural to man
Not quite. The article says: Nature works by cooperation and harmony; deliberate violence is found only among humans and brings only destruction.
questions.rationale: “Violence occurs only in the human world, not in the world of nature… only the peaceful method which nature abides by produces positive results.”

questions.q: A Companion explained taqwa by asking how one walks along a path lined with thorny bushes. What was the answer?
options: One runs through as fast as possible
Not quite. The article says: One gathers one’s clothes close and goes carefully on one’s way.
One gathers one’s clothes close and goes carefully on one’s way
Yes. Taqwa is this cautious attitude.
One turns back
Not quite. The article says: One gathers one’s clothes close and goes carefully on one’s way.
One cuts the bushes down
Not quite. The article says: One gathers one’s clothes close and goes carefully on one’s way.
questions.rationale: “‘I gathered my clothes close to me and went on my way’. Ubayy ibn Kaab said, ‘It is this cautious attitude which is called taqwa.’”

questions.q: With what words did the Prophet greet the new moon of Ramazan?
options: A prayer that it come “with peace and security”
Correct. The article calls Ramazan the month of patience and peace.
An order to store food
Not quite. The article says: A prayer that it come “with peace and security”.
A warning of hardship to come
Not quite. The article says: A prayer that it come “with peace and security”.
A call to prepare for battle
Not quite. The article says: A prayer that it come “with peace and security”.
questions.rationale: “O God, let the moon of the month of Ramazan appear on us with peace and security.”

questions.q: In the article’s image, what awaits passengers at “the airport of the Hereafter”?
options: All will be sent back to begin again
Not quite. The article says: Some will be stopped for questioning, others welcomed with greetings of peace.
Some will be stopped for questioning, others welcomed with greetings of peace
Yes. And the time of landing is not announced.
Only the first to arrive will be admitted
Not quite. The article says: Some will be stopped for questioning, others welcomed with greetings of peace.
All will pass through without any check
Not quite. The article says: Some will be stopped for questioning, others welcomed with greetings of peace.
questions.rationale: “Some will be stopped for questioning while others will be welcomed and led into Paradise… The time will come without any announcement.”

questions.q: A young man complained that his prayers for his problems went unanswered. How does the article answer him?
options: Worldly conditions are like an examination paper set by God; one keeps asking and leaves the choice to Him
Right. He knows what is truly good for us.
Prayers for worldly needs are forbidden
Not quite. The article says: Worldly conditions are like an examination paper set by God; one keeps asking and leaves the choice to Him.
His problems were a punishment
Not quite. The article says: Worldly conditions are like an examination paper set by God; one keeps asking and leaves the choice to Him.
He had not prayed often enough
Not quite. The article says: Worldly conditions are like an examination paper set by God; one keeps asking and leaves the choice to Him.
questions.rationale: “The ideal prayer would be ‘O God! Please grant me whatever is best for me!’ and then to willingly accept whatever is given.”

questions.q: Which prayer did the Prophet teach Aisha for the Night of Destiny?
options: “O God, make this night last”
Not quite. The article says: “O God, You are the One who forgives and You love to forgive, so forgive me”.
“O God, give me victory over my enemies”
Not quite. The article says: “O God, You are the One who forgives and You love to forgive, so forgive me”.
“O God, You are the One who forgives and You love to forgive, so forgive me”
Yes. Seeking forgiveness shows one’s smallness before God.
“O God, grant me wealth and long life”
Not quite. The article says: “O God, You are the One who forgives and You love to forgive, so forgive me”.
questions.rationale: “O God! Certainly You are the One who grants forgiveness for sins. You love to forgive, so forgive me.”

questions.q: The Prophet came out to tell people which night it was, saw two men quarrelling, and the knowledge was taken from him. What lesson does the article draw?
options: Good news should be kept secret
Not quite. The article says: Conflict, even in words, shuts out divine blessings; they come to a positive mind.
Conflict, even in words, shuts out divine blessings; they come to a positive mind
Well reasoned. Free of hatred and revenge.
The night is the same every year
Not quite. The article says: Conflict, even in words, shuts out divine blessings; they come to a positive mind.
Quarrels are best settled in public
Not quite. The article says: Conflict, even in words, shuts out divine blessings; they come to a positive mind.
questions.rationale: “Even fighting with words is enough to have the divine knowledge taken away… Positivity is the most important trait that makes a man worthy of receiving God’s blessings.”
